newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Junk jolted, high-grades sleep.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Junk jolted, high-grades sleep.

text.p: The U.S. high-yield corporate bond market was startled by weakness in the stock and Treasury markets on Friday, but investment-grade bonds continued their summer slumber undisturbed, traders said.
After shrugging off last Friday's Treasury sell-off and exhibiting a firm tone this week, junk bond prices showed signs of weariness Friday, slumping 1/4 of a point on average.

This week's volatility in the Treasury and stock markets also took its toll on closely watched junk bond mutual funds. AMG Data Services reported negative weekly cash flow numbers for the first time since late May.

"There is a little concern that there may be some follow-through (in outflows) because clearly, volatility in the dollar, stock, and Treasury markets can drive market-timers to pull money," said one trader.

He added, "I wouldn't be surprised if there are some professional market timers that, given the volatility, want to move into T-bills (out of junk bonds) and go relax in the Hamptons for the next two weeks."
Nevertheless, traders showed only mild concern, noting investor demand for new paper remained firm and strong credit fundamentals for junk bond issuers were still in place.
Some new issues showed signs of strength, notably IXC Communications Inc's $300 million junior exchangeable PIK preferred stock offering.
The deal, priced at par yesterday via Credit Suisse First Boston, was heard trading at 103 3/4-104 1/4 on Friday.
Conversly, prices on Fox/Liberty Networks LLC's $750 million two-part junk offering, weakened slightly on Friday after being priced by Merrill Lynch & Co on Thursday.
"The deal was upsized and most people got what they wanted. There is not much demand for the paper at this point," said one trader.

In secondary trading, prices on Brunos Inc paper continued to weaken as investors showed signs of concern about the supermarket company's recent sales results, traders said. The bonds were heard trading 93 3/8 after closing yesterday at 95-97.
In the high-grade sector, traders said prices of most bonds were unchanged on extremely thin volume.
